hero.description: COPE Visitor Centre is one of Vientiane’s most important context stops: a compact exhibition connects the history of unexploded ordnance in Laos with rehabilitation, mobility and the lives of people still affected today.
steps: Watch a documentary if time allows
Connect the exhibition to COPE’s rehabilitation work
hero.rhythmNote: Do not squeeze COPE between two monument photos. The centre is small, but the subject is heavy enough to deserve an unhurried hour or two.

chapters.label: THE LEGACY
chapters.title: The exhibition connects war history to present-day life
chapters.body: COPE’s visitor centre explains how unexploded ordnance continues to affect people in Laos decades after the conflict that left it behind. The strongest parts of the visit are not the objects themselves but the connection between contamination, injury, daily life and the long work required to respond.

chapters.label: THE RESPONSE
chapters.title: Do not leave with UXO as the only story
chapters.body: COPE is also about rehabilitation and mobility. The centre explains how COPE, the Centre for Medical Rehabilitation and partners support people with mobility-related disabilities. That shift matters: the visit is not only about a historical problem, but about practical systems that help people move forward.

note.label: ATLAS NOTE
note.text: COPE adds a layer that monuments cannot: it makes modern Lao history personal, current and connected to real rehabilitation work.

items.label: Time needed
items.detail: An hour works; extra time lets you watch short documentaries and read the personal material without rushing.

items.label: Entry
items.detail: COPE states that admission is free and donations are welcome.

items.label: Location
items.detail: Across from the Green Park Hotel; follow the internal road through the Centre for Medical Rehabilitation grounds.

items.label: Opening
items.detail: COPE’s official page currently shows conflicting closing times, so check the current hours before making a tight schedule.

faq.question: What is the COPE Visitor Centre about?
faq.answer: It explains the history and continuing impact of unexploded ordnance in Laos, alongside COPE and CMR rehabilitation work for people with mobility-related disabilities.

faq.question: How long should I spend there?
faq.answer: Allow one to two hours. The centre is compact, but documentaries and personal stories reward more time than a quick walk-through.

faq.question: Is COPE free to visit?
faq.answer: Yes. COPE states that entry is free and donations are welcome.

faq.question: Where is the Visitor Centre?
faq.answer: It is inside the Centre for Medical Rehabilitation grounds on Khouvieng Road, opposite the Green Park Hotel.

faq.question: Is this mainly a war museum?
faq.answer: No. UXO history is central, but the exhibition also focuses on rehabilitation, mobility-related disability and the people and services responding to that legacy today.
